subject: Audit & access log TTLs, export formats, and customer-driven deletion walkthrough
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medicorps.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediCorps Legal <legal@medicorps.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Log retention/export questions for upcoming audit

Hi Monica,

We have an external audit starting next month and the auditors have asked for a slice of access and audit logs for specific user activity windows (two 30-day windows spread across the past 12 months). We need:
- Exact retention windows for audit vs access logs (where "access" is auth and token events and "audit" is admin/role changes + tenant-level actions)
- Export formats you can provide (CSV, JSON, syslog stream?) and whether exports contain full raw events or are filtered/sanitized by default
- A short walk-through on how MediCorps can trigger exports and request deletions for specific customer data (GDPR/e-Discovery style) — auditors want an outline we can include in evidence.

Can you also tell us whether exports include IP addresses and whether those are redacted depending on region?

Thanks,
Raj
Head of Infrastructure, MediCorps

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medicorps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Log retention/export questions for upcoming audit

Hi Raj — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, details below and I've looped in Marissa (Product) for the format and runbook and Ben for procurement/turnaround expectations.

Key points:
- Retention: by default audit logs (admin/role changes, tenant-level actions) are retained for 24 months for our US tenants; access logs (auth/token usage, read requests) are retained for 12 months. These windows are configurable for Dedicated/Private customers (we can extend or shorten by policy).
- Exports: we can provide exports as newline-delimited JSON (recommended for fidelity) and CSV slices for quick review. For streaming handoff we support syslog over TLS and SCP/HTTP pull of compressed bundles. Exports contain raw event fields unless you request redaction presets.
- IPs and PII: by default IPs are included for US-region tenants. For EU/UK residents we apply IP pseudo-anonymization unless customer chooses to accept full export with appropriate legal controls.

Next steps: 1) Marissa will attach a sample CSV and a short runbook for initiating a one-off export and the API/console steps for requesting deletion of specific object IDs. 2) Ben will propose a turnaround SLA for 30-day and ad-hoc export requests (we typically do bulk exports within 72 hours for paid support tiers).

I attached a short checklist you can give your auditors. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute screen-share tomorrow to walk through the console export flow.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medicorps.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Log retention/export questions for upcoming audit

Hi Raj — attaching a small sample export and a one-page runbook (see attachments). A few technical clarifications and limitations to flag for the auditors:

1) Time windows: our export tooling supports arbitrary time-range slices but note that very long ranges (multiple years) will be chunked into compressed archive files (~100GB chunks recommended for performance).

2) Event fidelity: newline-delimited JSON yields full event payloads including contextual fields (ip_address, user_agent, request_id, tenant_id). CSV exports flatten the most commonly requested columns (timestamp, user, event_type, resource, ip_address) — use CSV for fast review, JSON for forensics.

3) Deletion workflow:
- Customer-initiated: MediCorps can request deletion for specific tenant artifact IDs through the Console > Data Exports > Delete request (requires owner auth). We record an SR ticket; deletion is executed in our cold storage getter and backed up by a deletion manifest.
- Platform-initiated: on request we can provide a signed deletion attestation indicating which objects were removed and when.

4) Redaction and residency: For MediCorps (US region), IPs are present by default. If you want us to remove IPs prior to handoff we can run a redaction job, but that will remove the raw IP field from the archive (and may complicate forensic timelines).

5) Audit trail linking: exports include request_id and parent_event_id so your auditors can reconstruct session chains.

If you want the runbook updated with a slice of your tenant (so auditors see a sample with your metadata), we can produce that — it will be an export of a 30-day window and require a signed export request form.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference

Raj — quick note on SLAs and logistics:

- If MediCorps is on standard support, ad-hoc exports of <200GB are processed within 72 hours; larger exports or signed evidence packages (with attestation) are on a 5-business-day SLA.
- For recurring audit needs we recommend a scheduled monthly export job (we can push to your secure S3 bucket) and a retention override for the involved windows. That reduces one-off costs.
- Cost: One-off export processing and attestation is billed as a professional-services line item; I'll send a short quote after we confirm the expected size and residency constraints.

If you want to proceed, Monica — please coordinate an export request with MediCorps and I'll fast-track the PS quote and SLA.

Thanks
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
